Note::contiguous¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::contiguous() const

Always Already Contiguous¶

contiguous() returns the same Note, unchanged. A Note stores its cells as a single flat offset table in row-major order, so there is no such thing as a non-contiguous Note to repack — every Note, including one produced by transpose, permute, select, or narrow, already has its cells laid out in reading order.

The method exists for parity with array APIs where a view can be strided and a later step needs a dense copy. Writing note.contiguous() in code ported from such an API is harmless — it costs nothing and changes nothing — but it is never required on a Note.

Example: A No-Op, Even After A Transpose¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.transpose(0, 1).contiguous()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3, 2], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "d"], 
  ["b", "e"], 
  ["c", "f"]
]

The transposed Note is returned exactly as transpose produced it — contiguous() adds nothing.

See Also¶

  • Note::transpose / Note::permute: axis reorders whose results are already contiguous.

  • Note::reshape: change the shape of those same cells.
